subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should this issue be solved as a lightweight read-tool binary-document fallback, or expanded into native document parsing?
rationale: Current source proves the read fallback gap, but choosing automatic parsing would add dependency, resource-limit, and untrusted-document security boundaries that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Use safe fallback in read
options.body: Return a structured unsupported-document message for known binary document formats in the shared read path and point users to dedicated document tooling.

options.title: Add native parsing to read
options.body: Implement PDF/Office extraction directly in read, but only after maintainers approve parser ownership, MIME scope, size limits, and security tests.

options.title: Defer to document-input tracks
options.body: Keep read unchanged and route all document handling to broader attachment, input_file, or provider-native file issues.

recommendation.title: Use safe fallback in read
recommendation.body: Return a structured unsupported-document message for known binary document formats in the shared read path and point users to dedicated document tooling.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal for the read-tool boundary and product-safe default choice is Peter Steinberger's agent runtime/read-tool work.
